newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa recoups losses in late NY-led rally.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa recoups losses in late NY-led rally.

text.p: London cocoa futures staged a late rally on Tuesday, recouping losses after stumbling to near eight-month lows.
Traders said speculators and trade houses returned to cover their shorts after prices in New York looked increasingly oversold and began to punch higher.
"Everybody assumed the market was going lower, but when New York started to go up they started to cover their shorts," said one trader.
Benchmark March cocoa broke through 910 stg support and touched a session low of 903 stg a tonne in early afternoon deals -- a near eight-month low on second month continuation basis.
It then quickly recovered and ended unchanged at 913 stg. Other positions were mixed.
Sterling was the driving factor behind the morning sales as it romped ahead to new four-year high of $1.6765. It then eased to trade at $1.6755 at 1750 GMT.

Traders said a strong New York close could help London's March to extend its recovery on Wednesday. But it could be difficult to vault a downtrend line that has provided rigid overhead resistance since October.

"I think a close above $1,375 on March would be encouraging," said one trader. Longer term targets were around $1,390-1,400, he said. The March contract in New York was trading at $1,372 at 1751 GMT. London's late rally had no foundations in physical news and traders said sentiment remained generally gloomy although an expected ride to the psychological 900 and then 880 stg on March did not materialise.
March was expected to confront the upper end of the downtrend line at around 922 stg.
Turnover totalled a healthy 7,784 lots and included switches and AAs. Phibro was said to be a good buyer of Dec/March at 36 stg, while Refco continued selling the outright March, traders said.
"It was a mixed bag on the close," said one trader.
Technically, March remains in oversold territory with a 14-day RSI of 28 percent.
Physical demand remains generally shallow and attention is now focused on November arrivals from Ivory Coast which may shed light on recent estimates.
